title: Weight Reduction of the Fin Box Rib Webs Between Ribs 4 and 9
abstract: Machining relief in the fin box rib webs between ribs 4 and 9 following the fatigue test read-across, taking eleven kilogrammes out of the empennage without touching the rib caps or the attachment fittings.

sections.reason: The full-scale fatigue test article passed its second lifetime with substantial margin in the fin box, and the read-across showed the rib webs between ribs 4 and 9 carrying reserve factors well above the design target. The programme has a standing weight reduction target of 90 kg on the CIRRANE-13 and this area was the largest single opportunity that did not touch a primary load path or a certified interface. No in-service finding is involved. The CIRRANE-11 fin sees a different gust spectrum at its shorter fuselage and was excluded from the read-across.
sections.description: The webs of the six ribs between rib 4 and rib 9 are machined with a pocketed relief pattern, reducing web thickness from 4.0 mm to 2.6 mm outside a 25 mm land at every stiffener and fastener row. Rib D5530116876335 is the pattern part and the shear tie D5530114423837 at each rib foot is retained unchanged. Screws AES932279K1 are re-used at the original pitch, and the rib-to-skin land is not altered, so no change is made to the fin skin panels or to the attachment fittings at rib 1. Revised detail is on drawings D55301104718 and D55301101338. The change is production-embodied only; the pocketing cannot be applied to an assembled fin box, which is why the retrofit route is a complete rib set replacement in zones 321 and 324.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 11.4 kg per aircraft on the fin centre line, moving the empennage centre of gravity 6 mm forward, which is inside the loading manual tolerance and needs no revision to the weight and balance data sheet beyond the basic empty weight entry. No electrical load change. The pocketed rib is interchangeable with the solid rib as a complete item but a mixed rib set is not permitted between ribs 4 and 9. The fin box internal inspection task gains a web thickness reference dimension.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00721 in September 2025. A retrofit route exists through Service Bulletin CRN-55-1004 for aircraft undergoing a fin box repair, but it is not offered as a fleet campaign because the downtime cannot be justified by the weight saving alone.

type_data.balance_impact: Empennage CG moves 6 mm forward, within loading manual tolerance
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00721, rib machining moved to the five-axis cell
